P.name: Petrion
P.blurb: You came through the sea wall with Peter of Amiens' company. Behind you are the ships; ahead are the hill where the emperor watched the assault, and beyond it some of the richest churches in Christendom.

B.name: Blachernae
B.sub: Henry’s palace and the land walls
B.blurb: Blachernae was the emperors' favourite palace, set against the great land walls. It is surrendering this morning. In a few days the gates beside it will fill with Greeks leaving the city.

G.name: The Great Palace
G.blurb: The Great Palace is the old heart of the empire: five hundred rooms, thirty chapels, and the most famous relics in the world. To reach it you pass the emperor's guard and the Hippodrome.

S.name: Hagia Sophia
S.blurb: The Great Church, Holy Wisdom, is the largest church in Christendom. Last night two Greek noblemen drew lots under its dome for an empire that neither could hold. This morning the marquis Boniface is claiming it.

H.name: The Golden Horn
H.sub: Quays, Latin quarters and the Exchange
H.blurb: The Golden Horn is the city's harbour: quays and warehouses, the old quarters where Venetians, Pisans and Genoese lived until last year, and streets of houses climbing from the water toward the Great Church. The richest families left at dawn. Everyone else is waiting to see what the Latins will do.

questions.title: The Postern
questions.meta: Shared question 1 · Monday 12 April, afternoon · Every choice ends the same way: you are through, and the defenders break.
questions.prompt: The walled-up postern finally gives, and the hole is barely wide enough for a body. Through it you can see the defenders packed into the lane beyond, with more on the wall above hurling stones down on the breach. You are first through, on hands and knees, and they have seen you.

choices.text: Draw your knife and charge them, roaring, before they can close on you.
choices.outcome: They had expected the hole to stay empty. One crusader coming at them with a blade and a bellow is enough. The front rank breaks, the rest follow, and they run like driven cattle while your company pours through behind you, shouting your name.

choices.text: Turn back to the breach and tear at the loose stones to widen it, calling on God and the Virgin to bring your comrades through.
choices.outcome: Stones crack on the wall beside your head while you work, but the hole opens, and a dozen men come through at once. The defenders see the numbers and give way. Your company credits the breach to you and to heaven, roughly in that order.

choices.text: Go for what the front rank has dropped in the mud: gilded shields, axes, a paymaster's satchel.
choices.outcome: The fighting moves up the lane without you. You come away with a gilded shield and a satchel of Greek coin. The men who did the fighting noticed where you were.

choices.text: Above the inner face of the gate hangs an icon of the Virgin, set there to guard it. Wrench it down and brandish it at the defenders.
choices.outcome: The defenders see their gate's protector in a Latin fist and lose heart. Your comrades cheer the trick. The priests in the host are less pleased with how you handled her, and you pry the silver frame loose before anyone asks for it.

questions.title: The Emperor's Camp
questions.meta: Shared question 2 · Monday 12 April, late afternoon · Every choice ends the same way: the emperor flees, and his camp on the hill is taken.
questions.prompt: Inside the wall, Peter's handful of knights and sergeants form up on foot. On the hill by the Pantepoptes monastery the emperor's scarlet tents stand open. Mourtzouphlos himself spurs toward you with silver trumpets blaring, then reins in halfway, as if waiting to see whether you will break.

choices.text: Hold your place in Peter's line, and let the emperor come or go as God wills.
choices.outcome: The line holds. The emperor turns back to his tents, then abandons them, and behind you someone breaks open a gate so the knights can lead their horses in. What you pick up in the camp you hand to your lord for the common stock, as you swore.

choices.text: Make for the chapel tent, where the emperor's campaign icons and a gilded processional cross stand unguarded.
choices.outcome: You strip the silver and stones from the icon frames and leave the painted boards in the grass. It is a good haul. Word of where it came from travels through the host faster than you do.

choices.text: Charge after the emperor's retreating guard and cut down the stragglers on the slope.
choices.outcome: The guard does not stand. You catch the slowest of them among the tents and come back with a captain's sword belt. The emperor is already gone into the city.

choices.text: Go straight for the tents: the coffers, the plate, the jewels.
choices.outcome: You are among the first into the pavilion, with its chests of plate and jewelry. You carry off what you can before your lords' men arrive to claim the rest.

questions.title: Constantine's Tomb
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · Holy Apostles · Tier: highest.
questions.prompt: The Church of the Holy Apostles is said to be even richer than Hagia Sophia. Here lie the bodies of apostles, the pillar at which Christ was scourged, and the tombs of the emperors. Constantine, who founded this city, lies here with his mother Helena. A single old monk keeps watch beside the great porphyry sarcophagus. Nobody else has found it yet.

choices.text: Break the seal and take the crown from Constantine's head.
choices.outcome: Under nine centuries of dust lies a crown. Whoever holds the crown of the first Christian emperor holds an argument no elector can ignore. The monk's cry carries through the church, though, and the Greeks will speak of this desecration for generations.
choices.item: The Crown of Constantine (+1 vote in the imperial election)

choices.text: Take the relics of the apostles from their shrines.
choices.outcome: You fill a chest with the bones of the apostles, wrapped in silk. Any church in the West would build a new chapel to receive them, and their abbots will remember who sent them.
choices.item: Relics of the Apostles (+1 vote on any committee)

choices.text: Strip the gold and gems from the other imperial tombs, but leave Constantine's sealed.
choices.outcome: The lesser emperors yield gold, pearls and stones. You leave the founder alone, which seems to satisfy your conscience more than it satisfies the monk.

choices.text: Kneel beside the monk and keep watch over the tombs through the night.
choices.outcome: No one disturbs the tombs while you watch. In the morning the monk gives you his blessing and a few coins from the alms box, and you leave with a story worth more than the coins.

questions.title: Manuel's Tomb
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · An abbey of the Petrion (the Pantokrator?) · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: In one of the great abbeys lies the emperor Manuel, in a tomb richer than any saint's. Beside it stands a slab of red marble, the stone on which Christ's body was laid when it was taken down from the Cross. The monks show you what they say are the Virgin's tears, still marked on its surface.

choices.text: Strip Manuel's tomb of its gold and stones.
choices.outcome: The tomb is everything they said. You take what can be pried loose and leave the old emperor lying in a stripped case.

choices.text: Claim the stone of the Deposition for your church at home.
choices.outcome: It will take a cart, a ship and a great deal of explaining, but the stone on which Christ lay is yours to send west. No relic in your country could match it.
choices.item: The Stone of the Deposition (+1 vote on any committee; must be shipped, so cannot be sold in the city)

choices.text: Pry the gems from the stone's setting and leave the slab.
choices.outcome: The setting was worth more than you expected. The monks watch you do it and say nothing at all, which is worse than shouting.

choices.text: Stand guard at the tomb so that no one strips it, and accept the monks' gratitude.
choices.outcome: Three parties of looters come and go while you stand there. The monks give you a meal and a small purse, and they pray for you by name.

questions.title: The Old Priest
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · The Pantokrator · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: The Greeks of the district stored their valuables in the Pantokrator for safety, and your comrades are ransacking the main church for gold. In a side chapel you find an old priest with a long white beard, sitting on an iron-bound chest. He says it holds only holy things and begs you to leave it.

choices.text: Threaten him with death unless he opens it.
choices.outcome: His hands shake on the lock. Inside lie relics wrapped in silk, each with a scrap of parchment naming its saint. You fill your arms and leave him weeping on the empty chest.
choices.item: A chest of relics (+1 vote on any committee)

choices.text: Speak to him as one Christian to another, and ask him to share what he guards rather than lose it to the men in the church.
choices.outcome: He looks at you for a long time, then decides that holy things are safer in your hands than in the hands of the men shouting next door. He opens the chest and chooses for you himself. Before you go, he asks your name.
choices.item: A chest of relics (+1 vote on any committee)

choices.text: Push him aside and take the gold and silver reliquaries. Leave the bones.
choices.outcome: The reliquaries are heavy and fine. The bones go back into the chest, loose, and the priest gathers them up as you leave.

choices.text: Leave him and the chest, and join the others stripping the main church.
choices.outcome: The main church gives up its candlesticks and plate. Behind you the priest has gone back to sitting on his chest.

questions.title: The Convent Gate
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · A convent of the Petrion · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: The gate of a convent is barred. Through the grille an old abbess offers you the convent's small treasury if you will keep the men behind you from breaking in. The men behind you say a barred gate means gold, and they are waiting to see what you do.

choices.text: Accept the treasury, and stand guard at the gate.
choices.outcome: The abbess passes a bag of silver through the grille. You turn and face your own comrades, and after some argument they go elsewhere.

choices.text: Refuse the gift, and stand guard anyway.
choices.outcome: You tell the abbess to keep her silver for her nuns. The men grumble and leave. That evening the story goes round the camp, and it does you no harm.

choices.text: Break in with the men.
choices.outcome: What happens inside is what the oath forbade and what Choniates would later lament. You leave with the convent's silver and a share in its shame.

choices.text: Take the treasury through the grille, then walk away and let the men do as they please.
choices.outcome: You have the silver. You don't look back at the gate.

questions.title: Guard of the Treasure
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · the days after 13 April · The collection church · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: The leaders have ordered all booty brought to a guarded abbey, and you are posted at its door with nine other Franks and ten Venetians. On the first night you watch two of your fellow guards slip gold jewelry into their sleeves. One of them catches your eye and holds out a ring.

choices.text: Take the ring and say nothing.
choices.outcome: It is a good ring. By morning there are several fewer pieces of gold in the pile, and nobody counts.

choices.text: Report them to the Count of Saint-Pol.
choices.outcome: The count does not wait for a trial. One of the two is hanged with his shield around his neck as a lesson to the host. Some thank you, and some will never trust you again.

choices.text: If the guards are helping themselves, help yourself properly.
choices.outcome: You fill a sack and get it to your lodging before dawn. Others are doing the same, which makes it safer and no less a theft.

choices.text: Refuse the ring and keep your watch.
choices.outcome: The guard shrugs and pockets it. You stand your watch to the end, and the pile you guarded is a little smaller in the morning anyway.

questions.title: The Cistern
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · Under the Petrion · Tier: lowest · Repeatable.
questions.prompt: A soldier swears he saw a Greek family carrying bundles down a stair into one of the district's great underground cisterns on the night of the assault. The stair disappears into black water among rows of columns.

choices.text: Wade in with a torch.
choices.outcome: Waist-deep and freezing, you find a bundle wedged at the base of a column: silver cups wrapped in a cloak.

choices.text: Wait at the head of the stair for whoever comes back for it.
choices.outcome: At dusk a man and his grown son come down with a lamp. You let them fetch the bundle, then take it from them at the top.

choices.text: Search the cistern-keeper's lodge instead.
choices.outcome: The keeper has fled with whatever he had. You find a few coins and a good knife.

choices.text: Mark the place for the commissioners collecting the booty.
choices.outcome: You tell the clerks where to look. They thank you without much interest.

questions.title: The Palace Yields
questions.meta: Shared question 1 · Tuesday 13 April, morning · Every choice ends the same way: Blachernae surrenders to Henry of Flanders, and his men hold it.
questions.prompt: At the gates of the Blachernae palace, Greek officials come out to Henry of Flanders and offer him the palace on a single condition: no one inside is to be harmed. Henry agrees and begins posting his own men on the gates and the treasury. You are near the front, and the doors are open.

choices.text: Push past the terms. Pull courtiers out of the line and search them for what they carry.
choices.outcome: You come away with rings and purses before Henry's sergeants pull you back. Henry has given his word, and he doesn't thank you for testing it in front of the Greeks.

choices.text: Stand on Henry's word, and see the people inside come out unharmed.
choices.outcome: You walk the line as the household files out, and you turn back two of your own comrades. Henry notices who kept his promise for him.

choices.text: Slip in by a side door before the guards are posted.
choices.outcome: The palace is huge and the guards are few. By the time Henry's men reach the upper rooms, you have already been through two of them.

choices.text: While everyone watches the main gate, break into the treasury of the palace chapel.
choices.outcome: Chalices, a jewelled Gospel cover and a censer go into your sack. The chapel's priest saw your face.

questions.title: The Crowns of the Old Emperors
questions.meta: Unique question 2 · Tuesday 13 April · Tier: highest.
questions.prompt: Deep in the palace, a strongroom holds what the emperors who lived here before left behind: crowns of gold and stones on cushions, jewelled robes of silk, collars and rings. Henry's men have not reached this corridor yet.

choices.text: Take the finest crown for yourself.
choices.outcome: A crown worn by emperors is more than gold. Whoever is chosen to rule here will want it, and will pay for it in lands or favour.
choices.item: An Emperor's Crown (a bargaining piece: worth one favour, a fief or 500 marks from the new emperor, at the GM's discretion)

choices.text: Pry the stones out of every crown and leave the gold.
choices.outcome: You come away with your purse heavy with stones. The crowns stay on their cushions, broken.

choices.text: Take the silk robes, which will sell anywhere in the world.
choices.outcome: They pack small and they are worth a fortune. You look like a pedlar on the way out, which is a reasonable disguise.

choices.text: Fetch Henry, and stand guard on the strongroom until he arrives.
choices.outcome: Henry looks at the room for a long time, then at you. He sees you rewarded from it, and he remembers your name.

questions.title: Friday at St Mary of Blachernae
questions.meta: Unique question 2 · Friday 16 April · Tier: high (in fama, not marks).
questions.prompt: It is Friday. In the church of St Mary of Blachernae, the Greeks say, the shroud in which Christ was wrapped raises itself upright every Friday, so that his form can be seen. The clergy are gone. The niche where it hung is open.

choices.text: Wait out the day in the church to see it rise.
choices.outcome: The light moves across the floor and nothing happens. The niche is empty. Whatever was there is gone, and nobody can tell you where.

choices.text: Search the church and the sacristy for where the clergy hid it.
choices.outcome: You find vestments, lamps and a pair of silver candlesticks, but no shroud.

choices.text: Take the gold and silver from the empty reliquary niche.
choices.outcome: The fittings are rich even with the relic gone. You leave the niche bare.

choices.text: Find the clergy who stayed and demand to know where it went.
choices.outcome: A frightened deacon swears he doesn't know, and you come to believe him. Nobody knows.

questions.card: Item card: The Lost Shroud. Every player at this position receives the card, whatever they choose. It reads: You looked for it. No one, Greek or Frank, knows what became of it when the city was taken.

questions.title: The Gate Tower
questions.meta: Unique question 2 · Tuesday 13 April · On the land walls by the palace · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: Where the palace meets the land walls, a gate tower stands empty, its garrison fled. A tower like this could become a lordship in the new empire, if someone holds it before the land is divided. Below, Greeks are already asking whether this gate will let them out.

choices.text: Plant your banner and hold the tower with your men.
choices.outcome: You post your men on the stairs and your banner on the roof. When the commissioners come round, the tower is written down against your name.
choices.item: A Fortress Claim (a tower on the land walls, to be confirmed at the partition)

choices.text: Hold the tower, and charge everyone leaving by its gate a toll.
choices.outcome: Families pay a mark or two, and the richer ones pay more. By nightfall you have a chest of silver and a reputation among the Greeks of Thrace.

choices.text: Hold the tower, and let the refugees pass freely.
choices.outcome: The gate stays open, and the line moves through without your men touching it. The tower is still yours.
choices.item: A Fortress Claim (a tower on the land walls, to be confirmed at the partition)

choices.text: Strip the armoury and move on.
choices.outcome: Crossbows, good mail and a chest of bolts. Someone else can be lord of an empty tower.

questions.title: The Table Laid
questions.meta: Unique question 2 · Tuesday 13 April · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: In a hall of the palace, a long table is laid for a meal that no one came to eat: roast meats gone cold, bread, fruit, wine standing in gold and silver cups. A handful of servants stand against the wall, waiting to find out what kind of men you are.

choices.text: Call your comrades in and feast.
choices.outcome: It is the best meal any of you has eaten since Venice. The story of the emperor's table goes round the camp for weeks.

choices.text: Sit the servants down and feed them first, then take them under your protection.
choices.outcome: They hesitate, then eat. When Henry's men come through, the servants are yours, and they show you which rooms are worth guarding.

choices.text: Send for the hungry from the streets outside, and feed them.
choices.outcome: The hall fills with Greeks who have not eaten properly in weeks. It costs you nothing but the meal you might have had.

choices.text: Sweep the gold and silver plate into a sack.
choices.outcome: The cups, the dishes and the salt cellars all go into the sack. The servants watch the meat go cold.

questions.title: A Family Under Henry's Word
questions.meta: Unique question 2 · 13–17 April · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: A Greek noble family who stayed in the palace under Henry's guarantee now want to leave the city, as the leaders allow. Soldiers in the streets are stopping anyone who looks rich. They ask you to walk them to the gate and offer you what they carry.

choices.text: Escort them, and refuse payment.
choices.outcome: You walk them through three streets of soldiers to the gate. The father tries again to pay you there, and you send them on.

choices.text: Escort them for the payment.
choices.outcome: They reach the gate safely, and you reach your lodging richer. It was a fair bargain, and they knew it.

choices.text: Take what they carry, and leave them to find their own way.
choices.outcome: They hand it over without a word. You don't learn whether they reached the gate.

choices.text: Hold them, and send to their relatives for a ransom.
choices.outcome: The ransom comes in two days. You let them go to the gate with nothing.

questions.title: The Imperial Stables
questions.meta: Unique question 2 · Tuesday 13 April · Tier: lowest · Repeatable.
questions.prompt: The palace stables are full of horses and mules the Greeks could not take with them: tall chargers, ambling palfreys, strings of pack mules. Nobody seems sure whether horses count as booty that must be handed in.

choices.text: Take a good horse for yourself.
choices.outcome: A palfrey fit for a bishop. If anyone asks, it followed you home.

choices.text: Take a string of mules to sell.
choices.outcome: Mules are always wanted, and these are good ones.

choices.text: Lead them all to the collection point for the common stock.
choices.outcome: The clerks write them down. Someone grumbles that horses are not cloth or silver.

choices.text: Ride out on one in a courtier's robe, with a lady's veil tied over its head.
choices.outcome: Your comrades laugh. The Greeks you pass don't.

questions.title: The Road Out
questions.meta: Shared question 3 · Saturday 17 April · Every choice ends the same way: the refugees leave the city.
questions.prompt: A storm is blowing, and a long column of Greeks is leaving by the gate: families carrying children too small to walk, a woman near her time, young women with mud smeared over their faces so no one will look twice. At the front, an official named Niketas Choniates is pleading with soldiers who are searching the refugees for gold sewn into their rags. Near the back, a gaunt old man in a single coat rides a donkey, and the people around him keep their eyes down.

choices.text: Help Choniates get his people through the gate unharmed.
choices.outcome: Near the church of St Mokios a soldier snatches a judge's young daughter from the column, and her old father falls in the mud crying her name. Choniates begs you and the men with you to remember your oath. You go after the man together, and when you threaten to hang him he gives her up. The column passes out of the gate.

choices.text: Look harder at the old man on the donkey, then seize him.
choices.outcome: The people around him cry out as you drag the donkey's bridle round. He is the Patriarch of Constantinople, leaving his city with no staff and no shoes. He does not resist. Whatever the leaders decide about the Greek church, they will now decide it with him in their hands.
choices.item: The Patriarch Taken (shared by every player who chooses B; see rule below)

choices.text: Search the refugees yourself, and roughly, for what they are hiding.
choices.outcome: Gold in a hem, a ring in a mouth, a silver cross under a tunic. You find what others missed by not being gentle about it.

choices.text: Ignore them. Their houses inside the walls are empty now.
choices.outcome: You let the column go and work your way back along the streets they came from. Half the doors are open.

questions.rule:
Rule: The Patriarch Taken (proposed). If any player chooses B, the patriarch has not escaped. He stays in the city under Latin guard.
Bonus. Every player who chose B gains +1 fama, already in the line above, and is named in the narration as having taken part.
In Phase Four. Whichever committee decides the church settlement may summon the patriarch. It may:
1. Press him to submit to Rome. This meets the endgame line "Greek Patriarch forced to submit to Rome" without needing a new candidate.
2. Keep him as Greek patriarch beside a Latin one, which is the dual patriarchate.
3. Depose him and appoint a Latin.
Otherwise. If no one chooses B, he leaves as he did historically, and the Greek church has a head outside Latin control.
Your call. I've given the capture no individual votes, so that it can't multiply with class size. Tell me if you want that changed.

questions.title: The Axe-Bearers
questions.meta: Shared question 1 · before dawn, Tuesday 13 April · Every choice ends the same way: the Varangians do not fight, and the road to the palace opens.
questions.prompt: Before dawn, at the Milion beside the Great Church, a company of the emperor's axe-bearers stands around a young nobleman named Laskaris. Many of them are Englishmen and Danes. Laskaris was chosen emperor by lot a few hours ago, and he is begging them to fight. They are asking what they will be paid. Your company comes up the street in full mail.

choices.text: Charge them before they finish bargaining.
choices.outcome: They are in no mood to die for a promise. They break into the side streets, and you catch the slowest. The way to the palace is open, and your name goes into the story of the morning.

choices.text: Call out to them in their own tongue: fellow Christians, the city is lost; lay down your axes and no one will harm you.
choices.outcome: Some laugh, but most lower their axes and walk away down the hill. A few come over to your banner. Nobody on either side bleeds.

choices.text: Outbid Laskaris. Offer them silver to stand aside, and take their pay chest as surety.
choices.outcome: They accept your promise and go. You keep the chest, and you were never going to pay the promise.

choices.text: Seize the processional cross and icons carried by the clergy beside Laskaris, and hold them up before the guard.
choices.outcome: The clergy scatter, the patriarch escapes in the confusion, and the axe-bearers take the loss of their holy standards as the end of the matter. The cross is heavy with silver.

questions.title: Through the Hippodrome
questions.meta: Shared question 2 · Tuesday 13 April, morning · Every choice ends the same way: you pass through the Hippodrome to the palace gates.
questions.prompt: The way to the palace runs through the Hippodrome, a racecourse a crossbow-shot and a half long, ringed with thirty or forty tiers of seats. Along the wall down its middle stand bronze men and women, horses, oxen, camels, bears and lions, so lifelike that the Greeks say they once moved. At one end sits a bronze Herakles so huge that a man's belt would barely go round his thumb. A few Greeks are hiding in the upper tiers.

choices.text: Marvel at it, and march on. Whatever is here belongs to the common stock.
choices.outcome: You stop long enough to look, as every Frank does who passes through, and then go on. Clari, gazing at the same bronzes, thought no master in Christendom could match them.

choices.text: In the imperial box above the track is a small oratory of icons. Pull them out to make seats and trophies for a mock race of your own.
choices.outcome: Your comrades race round the turning post with icons for prizes and a footstool of painted saints. The Greeks in the tiers watch it all.

choices.text: Drive the Greeks out of the tiers, and beat them for what they carry.
choices.outcome: They had little, and they give it up quickly. You leave the tiers emptier and yourself no richer than you hoped.

choices.text: Hack off whatever bronze and gilding you can carry from the statues.
choices.outcome: The statues are too big to take, so you settle for a gilded fitting and a bronze paw. The rest will wait for someone with furnaces.

questions.title: The Empress
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · The Bucoleon · Tier: highest.
questions.prompt: The Bucoleon has surrendered to Boniface on the promise that everyone inside will live. In an inner chamber the noblewomen who fled here are waiting. Among them is the empress Margaret, sister of the King of Hungary and widow of the emperor Isaac, with her small son. Another is the dowager Agnes, sister of the King of France. Margaret asks whom you serve.

choices.text: Take Margaret into your own custody as a hostage.
choices.outcome: She comes with you without a word, holding her son's hand. Whoever marries the widowed empress gains a claim on Greek loyalty that no army can buy.
choices.item: Empress Margaret (+2 votes in the imperial election for whoever holds or marries her; counts as "Greek empress" for Boniface in the endgame)

choices.text: Offer Margaret your protection, and carry her terms to Boniface yourself.
choices.outcome: You stand at her door until Boniface's marshal arrives, and you hand him her terms in person. She thanks you as an empress thanks a knight, and the marquis hears about it.

choices.text: Demand the ladies' jewels as the price of keeping the soldiers out.
choices.outcome: They strip their rings and collars into your hands. The soldiers stay out, this time.

choices.text: Bow, leave the ladies to Boniface's guard, and search the empty apartments instead.
choices.outcome: The apartments were left in a hurry. You find enough in them.

questions.title: The Regalia
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · The Bucoleon · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: In a robing room near the throne hall, the coronation vestments lie in their chests: a long mantle heavy with stones, a cloak worked with eagles made of jewels, scarlet hose and jewelled shoes, the crown, and a brooch that the emperor Manuel is said to have bought for sixty-two thousand marks.

choices.text: Take the whole set for yourself.
choices.outcome: No one can be crowned properly without these, and now no one can be crowned without you. The leaders will not forgive it quickly, and they will not be able to ignore it either.
choices.item: The Imperial Regalia (a bargaining piece: the GM rules what the next emperor will give for it)

choices.text: Keep the set together, and guarded, for whoever is crowned.
choices.outcome: When the time comes, the bishops find every piece where it should be. The new emperor knows who kept them.

choices.text: Pry the stones out of the mantle and the cloak.
choices.outcome: A fortune in stones, and two ruined vestments.

choices.text: Take only Manuel's brooch.
choices.outcome: It is small enough to hide in your fist and worth more than a county, if half the stories are true.
choices.item: Manuel's Brooch (worth 500 marks if sold; worth a great deal more as a gift to the right candidate, at the GM's discretion)

questions.title: The Holy Chapel
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · The Bucoleon · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: Through a door whose hinges are solid silver you enter the palace's Holy Chapel. Its pillars are jasper and porphyry, and its floor is white marble as clear as crystal. In its niches lie the greatest relics in Christendom: two pieces of the True Cross as thick as a man's leg, the lance, the nails, a phial of Christ's blood, his tunic, the crown of thorns, and the head of John the Baptist. An old Greek chaplain stands between you and them.

choices.text: Take the True Cross and the Crown of Thorns for yourself.
choices.outcome: You carry the holiest objects in the world out into the courtyard. Within an hour the whole host knows, and the bishops, the barons and your own comrades are shouting at you. They cannot agree what to do with you, and none of them will forget it.
choices.item: The True Cross and the Crown of Thorns (+2 votes on any committee; the endgame relic rules apply if they leave the city)

choices.text: Take a single thorn from the crown, and leave the rest.
choices.outcome: One thorn, sharp as a blade, wrapped in silk. The chaplain sees you take it and says nothing. A bishop at home would give a great deal for it.
choices.item: A Thorn of the Crown (+1 vote on any committee)

choices.text: Take the gold and silver reliquaries, and leave the relics on the altar.
choices.outcome: The reliquaries are worth a fortune by weight. The relics lie on the altar, bare, and the chaplain begins to gather them up.

choices.text: Stay with the chaplain, and guard the chapel until Boniface's men arrive.
choices.outcome: Two parties of soldiers come to the door and turn back when they see you. When the marquis's men arrive, the chapel is as it was.

questions.title: The Treasury
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · The Bucoleon · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: The treasure in this palace is past counting, and Boniface has set his own men over it. The guard on the vault door is from your own country, and he is bored.

choices.text: Bribe him, and take a chest.
choices.outcome: He looks the other way for the price of a good horse. The chest is heavier than the horse.

choices.text: Talk your way in as a messenger from the marquis.
choices.outcome: You walk in with a straight face and out with a small coffer. It is not stealing if no one asks, you tell yourself.

choices.text: Report the guard's slackness to Boniface's marshal.
choices.outcome: The guard is replaced, and the marshal learns your name. The treasure is a little safer for a while.

choices.text: Join the guard, and keep your hands clean.
choices.outcome: You stand watch through the night beside a fortune and go to bed with nothing.

questions.title: The Empress's Boat
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · first light, Tuesday 13 April · The palace quay · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: At the palace's own landing on the sea, servants are loading the last chests into a boat. They tell you that the empress Euphrosyne and her daughters sailed in the night with the emperor Mourtzouphlos, in a small fishing boat. One veiled young woman among the servants keeps her face turned away from you.

choices.text: Pull back her veil. She might be one of the daughters.
choices.outcome: She is a maid of the household, and terrified. The daughters really are gone. You have frightened a servant, and the others saw it.

choices.text: Seize the chests before the boat can leave.
choices.outcome: The chests hold the empress's linens, plate and a casket of rings she could not take in the night.

choices.text: Let the servants go, with what they have.
choices.outcome: They push off and row hard for the Asian shore. You stand on the quay and watch them go.

choices.text: Press the servants for where the emperor went.
choices.outcome: They say he means to join his father-in-law, the old emperor Alexios, in Thrace. You carry the news to the barons, who are glad to have it.

questions.title: Five Hundred Rooms
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · The Bucoleon · Tier: lowest · Repeatable.
questions.prompt: The palace runs on and on: five hundred rooms opening one into the next, every wall in gold mosaic, and thirty chapels large and small. Others have been through already, but the place is too big to empty in a day.

choices.text: Pull down the silk hangings.
choices.outcome: Bolts of silk, lightly used. They will sell well in the camp.

choices.text: Search the smaller chapels for anything silver.
choices.outcome: Lamps, a censer, a small cross. The chapels were not all found first.

choices.text: Find a quiet room, and claim it as your lodging.
choices.outcome: A room with a gold ceiling and a view of the sea, at least until someone more important arrives.

choices.text: Pry gold tesserae out of the walls.
choices.outcome: It is gilded glass, nearly worthless once it is out of the wall. You have spoiled a wall that took an emperor's lifetime to make.

questions.title: The Doors of the Great Church
questions.meta: Shared question 1 · Tuesday 13 April, morning · Every choice ends the same way: Boniface's men take the church and the patriarch's houses.
questions.prompt: Last night, under this dome, two noblemen drew lots for the empire, and the winner fled before dawn. This morning the marquis Boniface claims the Great Church and the patriarch's houses beside it, and his men are coming up the steps. You reach the doors with them. Every hinge and fitting on them is silver. Inside, Greek clergy and townspeople are still at prayer under a hundred hanging lamps.

choices.text: Clear the Greeks out of the church so the marquis's men can take it.
choices.outcome: They go, some of them shoved down the steps. The church is empty and echoing when the marquis's banner comes in. His captain thanks you less warmly than you expected.

choices.text: Enter as a pilgrim, kneel, and leave the Greeks to their prayers.
choices.outcome: You kneel among the Greeks under the dome. Nobody understands anyone else's prayers, and for a little while no one minds.

choices.text: Take the offering boxes and the candlesticks by the doors before the guards are posted.
choices.outcome: Coins, wax and silver. You are down the steps again before Boniface's men set the watch.

choices.text: Pry the silver plating from the great doors.
choices.outcome: It comes away in strips. The doors of the largest church in Christendom stand bare in places when the marquis arrives, and he wants to know who did it.

questions.title: The Healing Pillars
questions.meta: Shared question 2 · 13–17 April · Every choice ends the same way: you move on into the church.
questions.prompt: Along the aisles, sick Greeks are still coming to press themselves against certain pillars, which they say cure diseases of the kidneys and the side. By the great door hangs a small metal tube. The Greeks say that if a sick man puts it to his lips, it draws the sickness out of him. A line of the sick waits for its turn.

choices.text: Let them be, and stand by to keep other soldiers away from them.
choices.outcome: The line moves slowly. Nobody is healed while you watch, and nobody is harmed either. An old woman blesses you in a language you don't speak.

choices.text: Chip a piece off a healing pillar to take home as a relic.
choices.outcome: It takes a dagger and some effort. The Greeks around you make a noise you won't forget. Whether a chip of stone cures anything in Picardy remains to be seen.

choices.text: Drive the sick out. The church belongs to the marquis now.
choices.outcome: They go, the slowest helped along by your boots. In the scramble they leave behind the coins they brought for the clergy.

choices.text: Take the coins and offerings they have brought for the clergy.
choices.outcome: The sick pay you instead of the priests, because you leave them no choice.

questions.title: The High Altar
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: highest.
questions.prompt: The altar table is a slab of gold and precious stones fused into a single piece, fourteen feet long, the gift of an emperor long ago. A Greek sacristan tells you a story is already going round the city that the Latins have broken it up and shared out the pieces. It is still whole.

choices.text: Break it up, and take your share of the gold and stones.
choices.outcome: It takes a crew with hammers, and the gold comes away in pieces. If the story going round the city wasn't true this morning, you have made it true.

choices.text: Take the jewelled altar cloth, and leave the table.
choices.outcome: The cloth is heavy with gems and gold thread. The table stands bare.
choices.item: The Altar Cloth of the Great Church (sells for the marks shown; a debrief exhibit)

choices.text: Take the gold chalices and patens from the altar.
choices.outcome: The chalices will serve as wine cups at a feast in camp tonight. Choniates said the Latins would do exactly this.

choices.text: Guard it for the coming coronation.
choices.outcome: A new emperor must be anointed at this altar, and you mean it to be there for him. When Baldwin kneels before it in May, the table is whole.

questions.title: The Ciborium
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: Over the altar rises a canopy of solid silver, shaped like a bell tower, on silver columns and thickly overlaid with gold: tens of thousands of pounds of metal. A crusader engineer is walking round it, working out how it might be brought down.

choices.text: Help him rig ropes and pull it down.
choices.outcome: It is far too big for a day's work, or a week's. By nightfall you have one silver column off its base and a great deal of rope.

choices.text: Strip whatever gold overlay you can reach.
choices.outcome: You work along the lower edge with a knife. The gold comes off in curls, and the silver beneath shows through like a wound.

choices.text: Report its weight and worth to the commissioners collecting the booty.
choices.outcome: The clerks write it down with interest. It is too large for anyone to steal quietly, and now they know it is there.

choices.text: Persuade the engineer to leave it. The church needs its canopy.
choices.outcome: He shrugs and goes looking for easier silver. The ciborium stands over the altar, for now.

questions.title: Mules in the Sanctuary
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · the weeks after 13 April · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: The leaders have agreed that the churches may keep what they need for worship and must give up the rest. A party has come to strip the silver from the sanctuary railing, the pulpit and the gates. They want mules and asses brought right up to the altar to carry it away. One beast has already slipped on the polished marble.

choices.text: Bring the mules in, and help load the silver.
choices.outcome: The railing comes away in sections, and the mules carry it out through the nave. When the fallen beast won't rise, someone finishes it with a knife where it lies.

choices.text: Refuse to bring beasts into the sanctuary. Carry the silver out by hand.
choices.outcome: It takes three times as long and wrecks your back. The sanctuary floor stays clean.

choices.text: Take only what the clergy agree they can spare.
choices.outcome: The Greek sacristan points to what the liturgy cannot do without, and you leave it. The rest goes to the commissioners, as the leaders agreed.

choices.text: Load your own mule first, and leave before the commissioners count.
choices.outcome: One mule, loaded with silver, goes out a side door before anyone has written anything down.

questions.title: The Patriarch's House
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: The patriarch's palace beside the church stands open. The patriarch has gone, and his household is scattered. His rooms hold vestments stiff with gold thread, a library, chests of documents, and the seals of his office.

choices.text: Take the vestments and the plate.
choices.outcome: Gold-thread vestments sell as cloth of gold. The plate sells as silver.

choices.text: Take the patriarchal seals and archive.
choices.outcome: Whoever settles the Greek church will need to know what the patriarchs held, granted and owed. Now that knowledge is yours to share or to sell.
choices.item: The Patriarch's Seals and Archive (+1 vote on the committee that decides the church settlement)

choices.text: Claim the house for the Latin clergy of the host.
choices.outcome: You chalk the bishops' mark on the door. The Latin clergy are grateful, and they will need somewhere to live.

choices.text: Guard it until its people come back.
choices.outcome: A few servants creep back over the following days and find their master's rooms as he left them.

questions.title: The Keys of the Great Church
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · May 1204 · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: Weeks later, Venetian clergy arrive to take possession of the Great Church. The empire goes to the Franks, they say, so the patriarchate is Venice's. The Frankish clergy refuse to hand over the keys and have appealed to the pope. Both sides want strong arms at the doors.

choices.text: Hold the doors for the Venetians.
choices.outcome: The Venetian clergy take the church, as the agreement made in March said they would. They don't forget who stood at the door.
choices.item: Venetian Gratitude (+1 vote on the committee that decides the church settlement)

choices.text: Hold the doors for the Frankish clergy, pending the pope's reply.
choices.outcome: The Frankish clergy keep the keys for now and send their letters to Rome. They don't forget who stood at the door.
choices.item: Frankish Clerical Gratitude (+1 vote on the committee that decides the church settlement)

choices.text: Sell the keys to whichever side pays more.
choices.outcome: Both sides pay you something, and you end up despised by both, which is a common result.

choices.text: While they quarrel at the doors, slip into the sanctuary for the plate.
choices.outcome: Nobody is watching the altar while everyone is watching the doors.

questions.title: The Lamps
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: lowest · Repeatable.
questions.prompt: A hundred great lamps hang down the nave, each on a silver chain as thick as a man's arm and each holding twenty-five or more little lamps. The Greeks reckon every one is worth two hundred marks. There are plenty to go round.

choices.text: Cut one down.
choices.outcome: It comes down with a crash that echoes round the dome. Two hundred marks of silver, and a little less light in the church.

choices.text: Take a length of the silver chain.
choices.outcome: Easier to carry than a whole lamp, and still silver.

choices.text: Leave them burning.
choices.outcome: The lamps burn on above you. The Greek clergy who are still here see who left them alone.

choices.text: Take only the small oil lamps, not the great silver frame.
choices.outcome: A sack of little brass and silver lamps, and the great frame left hanging.

questions.title: Old Neighbours
questions.meta: Shared question 1 · Monday 12 April, evening · Every choice ends the same way: the quarter falls, and old scores are settled around you.
questions.prompt: With the army come Latins who used to live in this quarter until they were driven out last summer: Venetians, Pisans, Germans, Frenchmen. They know these streets and the people in them, and some have come back for revenge. One of them is dragging a Greek neighbour out of his house by the hair, and others are gathering round.

choices.text: Join them. These Greeks turned on the Latins before.
choices.outcome: The returning men welcome your sword. What follows is a settling of accounts twenty years old, and you take a share of the dead man's house for your trouble.

choices.text: Put yourself between them and the Greek.
choices.outcome: The returning men curse you for taking the side of the people who robbed them, but they won't fight a crusader in mail. The Greek's family pulls him back inside and bars the door.

choices.text: Stand back, let them settle it, and ask them which houses on the street are the richest.
choices.outcome: They know every door, and they tell you. You leave them to their business and go to the houses they named.

choices.text: Follow them to the parish church, where the neighbours have taken refuge, and help break in the doors.
choices.outcome: The doors give. Whatever sanctuary the church once offered, it offers none tonight.

questions.title: The House with the Low Porch
questions.meta: Shared question 2 · 13–17 April · Every choice ends the same way: the household leaves the city in the end.
questions.prompt: Near the Great Church, behind a dark doorway under a low porch, a crowd of Greek gentlefolk has taken refuge in a borrowed house. A Venetian in armour at the door tells you, in your own language, that he took it first and it is his. Behind him you glimpse their host: Niketas Choniates, one of the highest officials of the empire, whose own great house burned in last summer's fire.

choices.text: Accept his claim and move on.
choices.outcome: The Venetian nods, and you go. Inside, a family of Greeks breathes again, for now.

choices.text: Push past him to the household's icon corner, and strip the silver covers from the icons.
choices.outcome: The faces of the saints are left bare on their boards. The Venetian can't stop you, and the Greeks don't try.

choices.text: Call his bluff, beat him back, and take the household as your prisoners, with Choniates first.
choices.outcome: The Venetian is one man, and he gives way. You hold Choniates and his household for five days, until his friends pay a ransom. On Saturday he walks out of the city with the others. In the meantime he has told you more about the empire's tax registers than he meant to.
choices.item: Choniates Held (shared by every player who chooses C; see rule below)

choices.text: Strike a bargain with the Venetian: half of what the Greeks have, and the house is his.
choices.outcome: He agrees, because he can't hold the door against you, and he hates you for it. The Greeks pay. The house stays his.

questions.rule:
Rule: Choniates Held (proposed).
Bonus. Every player who chose C shares the ransom, already in the marks above.
Class-wide effect. The class learns what the empire's tax registers hold. When the partition is decided, the GM may treat the crusaders as already having the registers that the historical Latins had to commission assessors to compile.
No contradiction with Blachernae. The ransom outcome lets Choniates still leave on 17 April and meet the Blachernae players at the gate (B-Q3).

questions.title: The Best House on the Street
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · Tier: highest.
questions.prompt: Word has gone round the host that no one is to take a house until the leaders decide how to share them out. But the lords' men are already marking their masters' signs on the best doors. On this street stands a great house whose owner, one of the richest men in the city, left at dawn.

choices.text: Mark your own sign on the door, and hold it.
choices.outcome: You post a man on the door and your sign above it. When the houses are written down, this one is written against your name, and the lords' men have to go elsewhere.
choices.item: A Great House in Constantinople (a claim to be confirmed at the partition)

choices.text: Strip it before the lords' men arrive.
choices.outcome: By the time the marquis's sergeant comes to mark the door, there is nothing inside worth the chalk.

choices.text: Tell the poor knights and sergeants what the lords are doing, and lead them in.
choices.outcome: The news runs through the ranks like fire. The poor of the host go every man for himself, and this house is only the first of many. You have started something, and they know it was you.

choices.text: Wait for the allotment, as ordered.
choices.outcome: You obey. By the time the allotment comes, the best houses have long since been taken by men who didn't.

questions.title: The Exchange
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · Tuesday 13 April · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: Before the Exchange stand two bronze women, twenty feet high. One points west, and her inscription says that the city's conquerors will come from there. The other points to a filthy place and says that is where they will be thrown out again. Inside, where money-changers used to sit behind heaps of coin and gems, only a few remain, packing up in haste.

choices.text: Break open a money-changer's strongbox.
choices.outcome: It takes an axe and a little time. The box is full of gold coin and loose stones.

choices.text: Buy the changers' gems at a fraction of their worth as they flee.
choices.outcome: They know they are being cheated, and they take your coin anyway, because coin can be hidden more easily than gems.

choices.text: Escort the changers to safety, for a fee.
choices.outcome: You see three families of money-changers through the streets to the waterfront. They pay well, and they pay willingly.

choices.text: Have both inscriptions read to you, and carry word of them to the bishops.
choices.outcome: The bishops are pleased with the first prophecy and uneasy about the second. They remember who brought it.

questions.title: The Buried Silver
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: high.
questions.prompt: In a fine house, the Greek owner insists there is nothing left. The earth in the courtyard has been turned over recently, and he keeps not looking at it.

choices.text: Dig it up yourself.
choices.outcome: A jar of coins and a bundle of silver plate, a foot down. He watches you from the doorway.

choices.text: Talk with him patiently, until he decides it is wiser to show you.
choices.outcome: It takes an afternoon and a cup of his wine. In the end he digs it up himself, and asks you to leave him something. You do.

choices.text: Threaten him and his family.
choices.outcome: He digs. His children watch from the stairs.

choices.text: Leave him with what he buried.
choices.outcome: You walk out past the turned earth. Somebody else will probably find it, but not you.

questions.title: The Returning Owner
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · The waterfront · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: Your company has taken over a waterfront warehouse full of cloth and pepper. A Pisan merchant arrives with papers. It was his, he says, until the Greeks threw the Latins out last year, and he wants it back.

choices.text: Hand it back to him.
choices.outcome: He weeps, embraces you, and promises to remember you in his prayers and his prices.

choices.text: Keep it, stock and all.
choices.outcome: He goes to complain to the Doge, who has more important things to worry about. The pepper is yours.

choices.text: Split the stock with him.
choices.outcome: Half for him, half for your company. Neither of you is happy, which is probably fair.

choices.text: Buy his papers from him.
choices.outcome: He sells his claim for a promise of later payment, because a claim is worth little to a man the soldiers ignore. The warehouse is legally yours.
choices.item: A Warehouse on the Golden Horn (a claim to be confirmed at the partition)

questions.title: The Buyer
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: middling.
questions.prompt: A Greek dealer is going from billet to billet buying plunder, and he is not particular. He will take church plate as readily as household silver. Once it has left a church, he says, it is only metal.

choices.text: Sell him your church silver.
choices.outcome: He weighs it, pays fairly by weight, and wraps the chalices in sacking. Whatever he does with them, they are his sin now as well as yours.

choices.text: Sell him only household goods.
choices.outcome: Plates, cups and a lamp. He pays less than you hoped and more than you expected.

choices.text: Refuse, and warn your comrades off him.
choices.outcome: He moves on to the next billet, where someone will certainly sell. Your company thinks you are strange, but honest.

choices.text: Take his purse.
choices.outcome: He came to buy, and he leaves with nothing. Word goes round the dealers to avoid your street.

questions.title: The Burned Streets
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · 13–17 April · Tier: lowest · Repeatable.
questions.prompt: Whole streets here are ash, from last summer's great fire and from the fire set near the marquis's camp on the night of the assault. Families are picking through the ruins of their houses.

choices.text: Pick through the ash yourself.
choices.outcome: Melted silver, a few coins and a blackened cross. Enough to make the soot worthwhile.

choices.text: Make the families hand over what they have found.
choices.outcome: They give up their small finds. It isn't much, and it was all they had left.

choices.text: Help a family dig out what is left of their home.
choices.outcome: You spend the afternoon shifting rubble. They find their strongbox, and they insist you take a share.

choices.text: Move on to streets that didn't burn.
choices.outcome: There are plenty, and the pickings are easier.

questions.title: St Simeon (special path)
questions.meta: Unique question 3 · the days after 13 April · Not one of the thirty slots; open to any number of players in this region · Everyone who takes it shares the prize.
questions.prompt: You haven't come for silver. You and a few Venetians from the parish of San Simeone in Venice know that the body of the prophet Simeon lies in a church near the Great Church, and you mean to bring him home. The church is quiet, and its clergy are frightened. The leaders' guards are everywhere, looking for anyone who keeps back booty.

choices.text: Go by night, and break into the crypt.
choices.outcome: You lift the stone by lamplight and wrap the saint in a sail. Nobody sees you go, but you know what you broke to get him.
choices.item: The Relics of St Simeon (shared by everyone on this path; fulfils the Venetian secret objective)

choices.text: Bribe the sacristan to show you the tomb.
choices.outcome: The sacristan takes your silver and your promise that the saint will be honoured in Venice. He shows you the stair himself.
choices.item: The Relics of St Simeon (shared by everyone on this path; fulfils the Venetian secret objective)

choices.text: Carry him out in daylight, telling the Frankish guards he is a Venetian saint going home.
choices.outcome: It is a bold lie, and partly true. The guards wave you through, and the whole quarter sees the procession.
choices.item: The Relics of St Simeon (shared by everyone on this path; fulfils the Venetian secret objective)

choices.text: Hide him in a crate, and swear to the ship's master that it holds glass.
choices.outcome: The master doesn't ask twice. The saint sails for Venice packed in straw.
choices.item: The Relics of St Simeon (shared by everyone on this path; fulfils the Venetian secret objective)
